tips.comment: The favorite here has let connections down twice and is nothing special, which personally encourages me to look for an outsider with a chance. This is more of an idea in novice events such as this, where sometimes no one knows how their charges will run. Nothing at all was expected of Prodigal Son in May at Newbury, as most of the runners were from the elite stables. There are a couple in this race that may be half-decent handicappers, but that is it.

Marnier has his quirks, which include being slow away and hanging left in a finish. But this three-horse race looks like a penalty kick for him, and he should not be under too much pressure to win it from Oisin Murphy on Triple Gee.
There are plenty of question marks with regards to the odds-on favourite Marnier. I think it's worth siding with Triple Gee, the mount of Oisin Murphy.

Crepe Suzette's latest two runs have been on the all-weather at Wolverhampton. She was beaten into 2nd in a photo by a head in November and then won by a head in April. Her opening handicap mark looks competitive, and she should win on turf at Salisbury.

Happy to take on the favorite in this race as her best form appears to be on the all-weather. Oisin Murphy was in fine form at Windsor on Monday, riding four winners. Hopefully, he will be amongst the winners again now riding Patagonia Girl. In her last race, she was going well but faded towards the end of the race and finished fifth, so the shorter trip should help her cause. She is dropped a pound for this race, and Oisin Murphy gets to do the steering on Patagonia Girl for the first time. Murphy appears to be in really good form, and so hopefully he can conjure some improvement out of Patagonia Girl. If he does, then every chance of another winning ride.

Won here just over two weeks ago to break duck at the ninth attempt, although has come extremely close twice in the past. First-time cheekpieces may have made all the difference in length victory, and retains them again. Could make it a second win in a row if the three-pound rise has little effect.

Azahara Palace, a tough and consistent 5-year-old mare by Adaay, lines up in tomorrow’s Class 4 1m2f handicap at Salisbury. Trained by Hughie Morrison, she’s been admirably consistent throughout her career, boasting 4 wins and 8 placings from 18 starts??'a strike rate that marks her out as a genuine trier.
She’s no stranger to this course either, having won over this trip at Salisbury last autumn, showing a sharp turn of foot late on. More recently, she ran a solid third at Haydock in April, suggesting she retains her form and enthusiasm off a competitive mark.
Salisbury’s undulations and long straight suit her late-running style, and the forecast quick ground is right up her alley. With Morrison having his string in decent nick and Azahara Palace proven in this grade, she looks primed to run another big race.

Organic was a good flat racer until she changed yard to Neil Mulholland to go over jumps. Although the stats do not look good, it is mainly because she was running out of steam at the end of the races. So today's drop in trip should be just up her street. She returns to the flat today off a mark 6lbs lower than her hurdles race 10 days ago and 14lbs lower than her highest jumps mark. This well-bred daughter of Land Force and granddaughter of No Nay Never and Kyllachy has a 33% strike rate on the flat with three wins and two places from six races. Hopefully, she will slip back into her old ways and return to the winner's enclosure.
Completed a quickfire double in May in good style. Though up 8 lbs and moved to a class 5, had plenty in hand both times and should have more to offer in these conditions.

Reunited with Oisin Murphy and dropped to Class 5 again can help Grenham Bay return to being competitive in this contest. Has won over this course and distance off a higher handicap mark and that further highlights his chances.
Has won twice and placed four times in eight runs at Salisbury. Comes here on a nice low mark, a pound lower than when placing 2nd here last time out.

After finishing 2nd at Bath and then latest at Brighton, surely the Thames Boatman deserves to get his head in front. Both those runs were off a handicap mark of 74 and he remains on 74 for today's race. He has gradually dropped down in class to be more competitive and has a great chance here.

The trainer boasts a solid 42% strike rate at the track, and this is Sheena West's only runner on the card. The horse has had a couple of reasonable runs this season, but this has been the main target, you would think. Versatile on any ground. Each way chance.

A 4-time career winner between 6f and 7f, who made all to win over 7f for today's ride in a fast time at Lingfield just 10 days ago. Carries a 3lbs penalty but is only 4 and is still improving. Also has a win over this CD last September. Big chance on form.
Astrazar was last on debut at Ascot last time and should have learned plenty from that effort. The selection does need to improve on that effort but does seem to be well fancied to improve on that.
Making first race, but pedigree looks strong, coming from a former sprint/1m winner, and the stable is also in good form.
Too Darn Good was withdrawn from the Woodcote at Epsom last week and should find this race much easier. He ran reasonably first time out at Bath in 4th place, running on the outside.

I'm reluctant to bet against Clive Cox in a race that carries his name but SINJ seems to be getting the hang of this and is given consideration at this price. He clearly looks the best of the crop that have already run and with improvement expected she could come up trumps providing one of the debutants doesn't come in flying.
Eve Johnson Houghton is doing well with her two-year-olds, and Zavateri could go well drawn against the far rail at Salisbury.

Dandy G Boy will appreciate the return to six furlongs after weakening last time over seven furlongs here. He also has fallen again to his lowest mark of 62 and drawn against the far rail he should go close.

This looks like a good opportunity for Reporter to break his maiden. He has come down in the handicap and is also dropped into class 6 company for the first time in 9 races. He was runner-up last December rated 69 and put in a good reappearance in May when rated 68 only fading in the last half furlong over 7 furlongs. The fitting of a hood and the booking of Charles Bishop make you think connections are about to make good use of his new handicap mark of just 61.

Peregrine Falcon, which was highlighted on Springwatch last night! True, but I'm joking. Looks to have a major chance here for Patrick Morris, who does well here at 29%. He has enlisted Billy Loughnane, so that, to me, seals the deal.

All five career wins have come over today's course and distance. Only denied another win here by a half-length by the re-opposing Educate last time out. Seven pounds better off at the weights with that rival today and looks to have strong claims with top young jockey Billy Loughnane taking the ride. Another positive.
Won over a furlong shorter at Southwell on the 20th of April and likely to welcome the drop back to a mile and a half after racing over a mile and three quarters here when runner-up last month.
Finished close up in third at Southwell in April but disappointed when sixth at Nottingham earlier this month. Will probably be suited by the return to the all-weather here.
Two weeks ago, Blue Train was a promising 3rd in better company at Windsor. The selection has been going down the weights, so it is likely to land this at the expense of Classic Cause.
One of five horses in this race making a first start and has an impressive pedigree, coming from and close to several good winners. So, worth a shot at this price.

Anglesey Lad was heavily gambled last time with the gamble going astray. On Tuesday, he goes again at Wolverhampton without his usual headgear yet again. Good apprentice Taryn Langley claims a 7lbs allowance, which should be a positive. This race does not seem as deep as his last contest, so providing Anglesey Lad runs his normal self, a bold show with a gold medal being achieved on Tuesday. Our NAP selection of the day.
Kept on in the final furlong over this trip at Musselburgh on Saturday and is 9 pounds below his course and distance win back in November 2023. Turned round quickly for this.

Trusty Scout, trained by D. Shaw and ridden by Billy Loughnane, tackles the Highbet Traders Treble Odds Boost Classified Stakes over 1m1f104y on Wolverhampton’s Tapeta surface. Loughnane, Britain's top all-weather apprentice jockey and twice champion apprentice, brings in-form credentials to this ride.
A seasoned performer in AW handicaps, Trusty Scout recently ran well in this exact race on 12 June, staying on noticeably to finish 5th of 12, just four lengths behind. That run was a clear step back in the right direction following a break, and he’s shown strong consistency in this grade.
With a rating in the mid-40s, he's set up to be competitive right off the mark. Loughnane’s confident ride and ability to negotiate the bend and long home stretch at Wolverhampton may unlock another bold showing.

This A Watson-trained filly made a promising racecourse debut over five furlongs on good to firm ground at Yarmouth when beaten two lengths in second behind the highly regarded George Scott-trained Staya. With improvement expected, she can go one place better today with Hollie Doyle back on board.

This M Dods-trained filly has finished second in her last two races, the latest over five furlongs on good to firm ground at Wetherby eight days ago, when only beaten 3/4 length behind the M & D Easterby-trained favourite, Atomic Mass. So with P Mulrennan booked to ride, she can go one place better today.

Lima Sierra was beaten under two lengths by Novamay at Ripon when they were 4th and 2nd to Barmyblade at Ripon last month. She has since been 2nd behind Barmyblade again whilst Novamay was 2nd at Wetherby over five and a half furlongs having led. Lima Sierra could break her maiden tag on two pounds better terms with Novamay.

Crowns Lady, a progressive 4-year-old filly from the Edward Bethell yard, lines up in the 7f handicap at Catterick with Callum Rodriguez booked again??'a jockey who knows her well and has ridden her to success before. She brings a striking profile into the race with 4 wins and 16 placings from 16 starts, a level of consistency that’s hard to ignore.
She’s been knocking on the door lately, with a strong win at Wolverhampton earlier in the season and a close second at Beverley in April, where she was just reeled in late. Her mark remains workable, and her ability to handle varying ground conditions gives her versatility in how the race pans out.
Catterick’s sharp, undulating layout suits her running style, and with Rodriguez in the saddle and her form rock-solid, she looks like a reliable each-way option in a race that lacks standout depth.

Won 3 runs back at Doncaster in class 5 over 8f then stepped up to 8.5f at Nottingham again in class 5 finishing 3rd of 10 . Ran in 7f York handicap in class 4 finishing 8th of 22 last run 10 days ago an ok effort but dropping back into class 5 today should find this easier for the in form R.Fell yard .
In-form trainer James Owen is pretty astute at getting his new additions ready, and it will be no surprise to see Little Keilee putting in a much-improved effort.
Clasina remains a maiden but has been placed 3rd in her last two Class 5 handicaps. She looks to be turning things around and could go close again off her competitive handicap mark of 58.
Given much too much to do with last run, left poorly placed. Should do much better with a clear run. Great each-way chance at 8/1, nap each way.

A tricky-looking handicap where 16/1 shot Wichahpi looks overpriced. He ran well here last time over a shorter trip and will relish the extra furlong. He has a course win to his name and has dropped to a very good-looking mark.

The bare stats will show that the trainer's strike rate is poor this season, but that doesn't tell the true story. His horses are going really well right now, with stacks of them placing. The 5lb claimer associated with the yard is also good value for his claim, and the horse's opening handicap mark of 70, along with the jockey's claim, makes this outsider worthy of a second look. The placed effort over C&D has clues that she can go close off this mark, but the real key will be the first run on softer ground since her sire produces many horses that revel on it. I'd expect any further rain would see her price contract from the current 25/1.

Vibrant Pearl got up in the final furlong to pass Radio Star at Pontefract but got beaten herself by Maddelina, getting up by a head near the line. Two 2nd places for Vibrant Pearl and three 2nds and a 3rd place for Radio Star. One of them should win this time, and Vibrant Pearl probably has more potential for improvement.
Second on debut last term but only managed fifth when reappearing this season. Although that was a decent effort, so could be there or thereabouts.

Solid Bond, a 3-year-old bay filly. This will be her first run for 406 days after only running twice as a 2-year-old. Worth taking a chance with a 3lb claimer on board, and she showed form on her first start on heavy.

Sunny Orange came to hand at this time of year last season when a close 2nd in this race and followed that by a five and a half length win at Beverley ten days later off a mark of 56 which pushed him up to a peak of 64. Now back on only 53 he should be competitive again.
Miss Calculation is a course and distance winner but hasn't won for a while. Looks on an attractive handicap mark, and this could be the day at big odds.

A course and distance winner 3 races back and runner-up next time out. Not suited by the step up in trip here last time out over 2 furlongs further and much better over this trip. Wears the first time cheekpieces today, which could have a positive impact too.

A solid 3rd last time out. The jockey booking of Hollie Doyle catches the eye, and I believe she is having her 1st run for the stable. Solid each-way contender, and the horse is versatile on the ground and can make a solid each-way case here.

Prince Of Achille has been poor the last two times, but I think we will see an improved effort today now upped to 12f. From his six turf starts at this trip, he has never been out of the frame, and he ran well on his only start at the track. He is worth an each-way interest.

Kalganov has been a slightly weak finisher in his last three races over seven furlongs but has finished 2nd of 6, 4th of 13 and 2nd of 10 but has fallen to his lowest handicap mark of 55 having arrived from France in August 2022 and been given an initial mark of 95. Should go close again.

Happy to take the front of the market on here. Miss Rainbow improved for the visor last time but is up 2f in trip. Dods's horses are really struggling, so happy to oppose Kalganov too. Bird Of Play has run mainly on the all-weather since joining Liam Bailey, but he looks to be better on turf. His last run was a little more promising. The 3rd and 4th from that race won on next starts, so it may have been a decent race for the grade. He won off 68 a couple of seasons ago, and if the blinkers can spark him up, he's very well handicapped.
One to keep on the right side. Course and distance winner, jockey in great form, should be given serious consideration. Will be there at the business end of the race.

Cosmic Soul was beaten a nose by Zephlyn over course and distance two weeks ago when he was coming off a 154-day break. He should go close and get his revenge on Zephlyn on one pound better terms. Joe Fanning takes over the ride.

A beaten favourite over a furlong further at Carlisle 11 days ago in a slowly run apprentices race. Should benefit from the more experienced hands of Joanna Mason in the saddle and a couple of likely front runners should give him a much truer pace.

A 6-time career winner, 2 of them came at this track. The last one came over this course and distance back in August of last year. Ran well when a close-up third over this course and distance last month on seasonal return. Should strip fitter this time and runs off the same mark today and looks capable of a bold show.

The outsider of the field, Fleur De Mer, had almost a year off the track before his run in May, where he not surprisingly finished down the field. He looked progressive in his time with Hugo Palmer, and I think the soft ground and the run will bring out the best in him.
Market House has won three times on the flat and has got close to winning his first hurdle race, being beaten only a head last week at Market Rasen. Sean Bowen takes over to get the win on the board.

There was definite promise on his fifth-placed handicap bow at Leicester last year and we've seen this trainer gain wins out of ex-Simon Earle horses since training from the same yard. Hopefully the step up in trip will bring about some improvement as well.

It is fair to say that she was less than fluent in the jumping department here last month, but I liked her finishing effort to finish sixth. The application of first-time cheekpieces looks like a good move, and I just wouldn't be surprised to see her outrun her odds.

Gold Link finished in 2nd place in his last four hurdle races before going chasing in May 2023, where he won twice before regressing. After a poor jumping display last time, he switches back to hurdles, and he should have every chance of a win against She Is For Me Boys, who won here last month but was helped by the fall of a challenger at the last flight, who also brought down a closing rival, leaving her clear.

The model I run suggests Everest can win this one. Everest lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 8-runner field and goes out carrying the joint lowest weight. Freddie Mitchell on board relieves a further 5 lbs, which is helpful over this 2m 3f trip. Hasn't run in 160 days, so will need to run fresh. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Won 3/3 this year at C&D and going and clearly found his niche, but I don't think he's hit his ceiling yet. Won the last race going away when coming from the back of the field against similar types, including Summer In Milan. Mitchell takes off 5lb and the yard is in form (6/29, 21% last 14 days). Another positive performance in advantageous conditions likely.

It was just the second start over fences for Summer In Milan when beaten 10 lengths by Jack Sparrow Grey here 16 days ago. He is 8 pounds better off with that rival today, and on paper, weight alone may not be enough to reverse the form. However, he was not given a hard time when beaten and could have been closer and jumped right at a few fences. If the visor going on keeps him true and he comes on for the experience, then he looks the value bet to finish in front of the likely favorite today, which should be enough.

The model I run suggests Ryder's Rock can win this one. Ryder's Rock lines up here with a comparably high RPR but has an official rating leaving him very well treated off this mark. Carries 1 stone 7 lbs less than the top weight and current market favorite Jack Sparrow Grey. Ryder's Rock has shown signs of form. Won last time out in the first run since a recent wind operation and looks to go out and progress from that same level of ability to win here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Though Henry Box Brown is returning from a break and could possibly need the run, with the Evan Williams yard in good form, he looks sure to run well. With luck in running and jumping, he could possibly return with a victory.

4 times a winner in 11 races over fences, including one over course and distance off a 5 pound higher mark under today's jockey in September 2024. Will strip fitter for 2 recent runs following an absence of 163 days.
Onethreefivenotout got his first win over fences at Newton Abbot last time out and should be able to cope with a six pound rise in his handicap mark to follow up at Fontwell.

The model I run suggests Belgarum can win this one. Belgarum lines up here as the youngest horse of this 5-runner field and has a comparably high RPR in a tightly bunched field. Goes out with the second lowest official rating and therefore the second lowest weight to carry. Belgarum has won at this track before and is also a previous distance winner. Hopefully, the amalgamation of both of those bodes well to get the course and distance winner tag. Comes here in reasonable form with a first 27 days ago and looks to repeat the job. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Man Of The Sea can win this one. Man Of The Sea lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 6 runners here and has an official ranking that is the second lowest. That results in him going out carrying the second lowest amount of weight. The early market pricing suggests this is a fairly open race, but Man Of The Sea is one of only two horses to have shown any form coming into this. Man Of The Sea has figures of 122-43 and that last placing coming only 19 days ago. Man Of The Sea is also one of only two who has previously won this distance. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator primarily due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation, but also that 3.75 is a fairly short price already. This translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

Chicago Storm has been in good form since switching yards this year and has won twice from 5 hurdle starts. Last seen when on the level at Bath over 10f in April, finishing 3rd of 7, and now switches back to brush. Goes well for 7lb claimer Robbie David and can go close in a trappy little affair.

Al Arrivee looks very solid for this. She ran a very good race first time out last October, and she should come on for that. She is related to Gold Cup winner Al Boum Photo, so some improvement is very likely.

The model I run suggests Crossbar Getaway can win this one. Crossbar Getaway has a comparably high RPR to the rest of the 16-runner field and does not get penalized for it in the weights. All horses line up with the same amount of initial weight. Comes here in decent form and ran a good second only 10 days ago. Quick turnaround but looks to go one better. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

NELLA FANTASIA was well punted on her debut and many popular in the market can be worth siding with next time out including in this Bumper sphere. As a five year old mare she could be approaching the peak of her ability now and she seems likely to step forward on the back of her front running first effort. Again worth a market check.

Had some fair form in bumpers before switching to hurdling on her last two starts. Performed well at Sligo when 4th on her first start for 6 months. Connections go back into bumpers here with her but she looks a strong player despite that.

Wide margin point winner Quantum Boy disappointed on debut in a Punchestown bumper last month when only 6th. He should improve greatly for that, and with an extra 2 furlongs likely to help, he can make a winning hurdles debut.

The model I run suggests Bearami Creek can cause an upset here. Not fancied at all by the early market. Lines up with the second highest RPR of the larger 16-runner field. Looks well treated on the weights, where half the field carry 11-12 and the other half carry 11-5. Jake Coen on board lightens another 3 lbs, so the total weight being carried is 10 lbs less than the top of the market. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, largely due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Lightkeeper can win this one. Lightkeeper lines up here with the highest RPR of the 8-runner field and doesn't look overly penalized for it in the weights. Has been pulled up the last 2 times when out but won the two before that, but was attempting to go up in trip there. Back to the same distance of 2m 3f as the 2 wins came. Finn Brickley on board relieves a further 7 lbs in weight. Model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

A 3 times winner on the flat who finished a 5 lengths third in a claimer over 2m4f at Clonmel last month. Was traveling well there 2 from home so the drop back to 2m2f may suit better and could go close here with a good round of jumping.

Iorens is an ex-Skelton horse who cost £100,000 and is just a 7-year-old. Best runs on form have been at this sort of trip and on good ground. Was rated 109 over hurdles but seemed to lose his way and went pointing to re-find himself. All six point runs this year were 3m and this will be the second run for the new yard. Has it in him to cause a surprise here and long odds are worth a small stake.

The model I run suggests Cornmarket should win this one. Cornmarket lines up here with a comparable RPR to the top-ranked horses and an official ranking leaving him well treated off this mark. Ran this 2m 4f distance at Sligo and won only 28 days ago, so looking for a repeat performance here. Alan King on board relieves a further 7 lbs over the distance, and that is helpful. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator primarily driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

Ladiam's only win came over course and distance in a maiden hurdle back in August 2022. She is still running respectably and ran 2nd of 13 at Ballinrobe a fortnight ago. She has only been raised a pound to a mark of 92.
His two best efforts have been over this sort of trip and he is nudged up a couple of pounds after placing last time. No world-beater, but he is certainly capable from this sort of mark.

Cois Fharraige had shown little in 6 starts for Norman Lee, but there was definitely promise on debut for Gavin Cromwell here last month when 5th of 15, beaten just over 7 lengths. He is off the same mark here, but his useful apprentice claims 7 lbs, so he looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

A 2-time winner over hurdles whose last win came back in 2021. Showed some promise last year, finishing in the frame 4 times, including a close second here over a furlong shorter last July. Is now on a very handy mark, but much depends on fitness levels first time out this season, though the trainer had a Listed hurdle winner last month, and Craic Eile could go well here each way with 5 places.

I’m certainly not suggesting that EOIN MCCARTHY’s 5-year-old mare CHAPTER THIRTY is a winner in the making, but she doesn’t look like a 40/1 shot either (in my humble opinion). Rome wasn’t built in a day (or so I’ve been told), and this daughter of JUKEBOX JURY, while not setting the world alight, has shown steady improvement in each of her handicap runs, progressing by at least 10 lengths each time. In fairness, had she not jumped the second last like a bag of hammers, she would’ve finished closer at Limerick 12 days ago. She’s been dropped 3lbs for that run and, this time, could benefit from the services of a 7lb claimer in the form of Calum Hogan.
From a pedigree standpoint, this is the right trip and going for her, and with a career best coming at Tipperary (a left-handed, sharp track) in a maiden contest where she was staying on, this course could play to her strengths. The 40/1 price tag is certainly inviting - though I doubt I’d feel the same if she were going off at 10/1 - but I’m happy to play small in the hope she continues to progress, running near bottom weight.

The model I run suggests Kates Choice can win this one. Kates Choice lines up here with the second highest RPR of a large 16-runner field. All horses, bar a few, go out carrying the same weight, so Kates Choice is not penalized for the higher potential. Tries the tongue strap for the first time, and if the headgear makes a difference, should get over the line first. Last ran 10 days ago, so race fitness isn't a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.
Has started career with a pair of sixth places but is nicely weighted here due to jockey choices and could show promise if ground suits and cheekpieces work.

Nashville Notions has been steady, if not spectacular, of late with a string of middling to top 50ish% of the field finishes. But the shorter trip here, I think, will suit much better with staying power being an issue in the last few starts.

With no forecast rain on Tuesday, conditions should be dry enough for Ballycommon Chapel to show her best off her lowly mark of 85. Although a long-standing maiden, her last two runs were good enough to suggest she should go close, but her best form is restricted to good going.
Leitzel has decent form in the last at this track. After having met traffic problems last time out when coming a 3 lengths 3rd at Ballinrobe, it all points to another good run up just the 1 lb.

Bowgate Street won over course and distance last October and looks interesting again in this Sligo handicap hurdle. She has finished runner-up in her two starts before that, before winning off a mark of 89. She was then unplaced at Gowran off 95 in her final start last year. She returned off the same mark at Tipperary last month when running well before fading in the straight. She should be fitter here and looks a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.

TEA IT IS is an 8-year-old gelding trained by Denis Hogan, who has been lightly raced in recent years. His most recent performance at Limerick, just 12 days ago, was particularly encouraging, as he appeared much fitter compared to his previous outing after a lengthy 623-day absence. The son of the talented sire ALKAASED, a Group 1 winner, should benefit from the drop in trip, but it's the return to a sharper, more familiar track that truly catches the eye. His best runs have consistently come at tracks like Sligo, where he most recently finished 3rd, just 1¾ lengths behind the winner, off a mark of 89 - 18lbs higher than his current rating.
The addition of Gary Noonan aboard is another factor in his favour, with the jockey’s 5lb claim taking some weight off his back. The yard seems to be coming to form as well, with Hogan posting a solid 20% win strike rate over the last month. Given his improving fitness, course form, and the support of a capable jockey, TEA IT IS looks an appealing 20/1 shot, with a strong chance of hitting the frame.

A very open handicap hurdle of two miles with few coming into the race in strong form. The handicap is mostly quite compact too so Kalanisi Dubh is the choice running off a mark of 94, 2lbs higher than for last of two wins from 20 goes in hurdle competition. Those wins were both over the short trip on soft and heavy ground so forecast rain is providential. Jake Coen claims 3lbs for trainer Seamus Fahey. Strange sort of form: always well off the pace and sometimes turns up to stay on late. Probably has a chance at this fairly modest level of competition.
Ran a decent race on handicap debut last month. Can come on for that run. Drops back in trip, which will be a plus. Acts on any surface, so rain that's expected will not be an issue.

Makes a quick switch to hurdling for this yard after just two starts in novice company. Those have resulted in midfield finishes but haven’t been devoid of promise. Handicap mark looks a little high based on what we’ve seen so far, but improvement could be forthcoming. Interesting runner.
This looks like being a wide-open race, and there are plenty with chances. I prefer the chances of Mags Nelson, who won last time out at Tramore, and a run like that would be good enough here.

Ilbdare was one of two horses who went a good way clear of the remainder over course and distance 28 days ago. The five-year-old was well backed that day and the money is coming again. He was 15 lengths behind Our Zebo previously but meets that rival (who has won since) on 14 lbs better terms today. Looks to have good ground conditions to suit. In-form amateur jockey AP Ryan (SR 38%) claims 7 lbs. Played at odds of 7-2.

The model I run suggests Yorkshire Escape can win this one. The model result has been driven by Yorkshire Escape having the highest RPR of the larger 15-runner field but an official ranking leaving him joint bottom in the weights. The jockey on board claims a further 7 lbs and had a run out 11 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. There's not much form on offer in this contest to go by, but hopefully progression here gives an opportunity. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
